subject: Private observability: SIEM adapter, traces & export for Velox (on-prem/VPC)
messages:
From: Daniel Park <dpark@veloxsec.com>

Cc: ops@veloxsec.com

Subject: Private observability for on-prem deployment - high level questions

Hi Hiro,

Thanks for taking this on. We're starting the SIEM onboarding for our initial Redwood private deployment (Velox is running in a locked-down VPC with an on-prem data collector). Before we schedule a call I wanted a concise picture of the options so we can scope our firewall and compliance tasks. High-level asks: 

- What evidence export patterns does Redwood support for private deployments? (syslog/tcp, HEC, S3 push, agent pull, collector relay)
- How are traces surfaced to our APM/SIEM? Is there a direct OTLP/Zipkin forwarder or do you recommend using the OTel collector on our side?
- What network egress/ingress ports/CIDR should our infra team open for an initial proof-of-transfer?
- Any recommended retention/rotation settings or recommended sample payloads for SOC 2 evidence?

We've attached our SIEM requirements doc and a small sample of app logs. Would appreciate a short ops-runbook or checklist we can hand to our network/security team.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Park
Head of Platform Security — Velox Security

From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Private observability for on-prem deployment - high level questions

Hi Daniel —

Thanks for the doc and samples. Below is a concise ops-first summary and a proposed next step (15–20 minute sync + checklist handoff):

Overview of supported export patterns (private mode):
- Splunk HEC (HTTPS) to your collector: recommended for structured logs and metrics. Redwood can push via a dedicated forwarder inside the customer VPC.
- Syslog/TCP (RFC5424) to on-prem SIEM collectors: supported via our forwarder with TLS termination.
- S3-style push (signed, ephemeral) for bulk evidence exports (audit snapshots / evaluation payloads).
- OTLP/HTTP for traces: we support pushing spans directly to an OTLP endpoint; alternatively, customers commonly run an OTel collector inside the VPC and point Redwood at localhost:4318 to avoid cross-region egress.

Network & auth patterns (short):
- Preferred: deploy a lightweight Redwood forwarder in a private subnet with egress only to your collector IPs over mTLS or HEC tokens.
- Ports: HEC/TLS 443 (HEC over HTTPS), OTLP/HTTP 4318 (if using direct), Syslog/TCP 6514 (TLS-wrapped syslog) — we can tunnel/translate if you have port restrictions.
- CIDR/IPs: for proof-of-transfer open outbound to the collector appliance IPs for initial testing. We will provide a minimal set of IPs for the forwarder only.

Trace and sampling guidance:
- Default: 1% sampling for high-volume endpoints; keep 100% for auth/financial routes for auditability.
- Use prefix-based caching on the Redwood runtime to reduce tokenization noise in logs used for trace reconstruction.

Evidence & retention:
- SOC 2-friendly exports: we recommend weekly signed S3 snapshots with SHA256 manifests retained for 90 days (longer if you need).
- For immediate audits, we can produce a focused evidence bundle (logs + span links + release/tag) for a requested time window.

Next steps: 1) propose 30-min ops call this week to align on collector type (Splunk vs on-prem SIEM) and authentication (mTLS vs token), 2) we’ll hand over a minimal firewall checklist and a forwarder config template.

Attaching a short checklist template and our suggested forwarder config excerpt.

Cheers,
Hiro
Hiro Tanaka
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private observability for on-prem deployment - detailed ops checklist

Daniel — quick technical checklist from infra/observability side (actionable items your networking team can use):

Network & firewall (minimum for POC):
- Allow outbound from the forwarder host to these endpoints/ports:
  - <collector-ip-1>:443 (HEC over HTTPS)
  - <collector-ip-2>:6514 (syslog/tcp-tls)
  - 127.0.0.1:4318 if running local OTel collector (loopback only)
- If you cannot open 443 outbound, we can run a TLS relay on an allowed port inside your perimeter.
- Keep DNS for the forwarder resolvable internally; avoid public DNS for evidence push endpoints.

Authentication & certs:
- mTLS preferred for forwarder -> collector (we can provision CA-signed certs or accept your internal CA).
- HEC token acceptable for Splunk; rotate every 30 days for audit hygiene.

Logging/format (mapping):
- Structured JSON logs recommended; include fields: trace_id, span_id, service, env, request_id, timestamp_iso.
- If using syslog, use RFC5424 structured data block with JSON payload.

Tracing hooks & sampling (practical):
- Redwood runtime emits spans with service naming: redwood.<model>.<deployment>. Configure trace processor to drop internal debug spans before forwarding.
- Suggested rate: 2% global, 100% on login/payment endpoints, 10% on search/autocomplete endpoints.

Evidence export & audit artifacts:
- For SOC 2: retain original raw logs + parsed evidence for 90 days. We will append a manifest file that includes SHA256 checksums and the Redwood release tag.
- For on-demand audits, we recommend collecting a 72-hour evidence window (logs+spans+tokenized prompt snapshots) zipped and signed.

Operational runbook items (short):
1) Deploy forwarder in private subnet with IAM role (if using S3 push)
2) Point OTel to localhost if you want local aggregation
3) Run initial 24h transfer with verbose debug logging and a follow-up validation run to confirm field mapping
4) Provide list of collector IPs and preferred auth method to Redwood SRE

I'll paste an excerpt of a forwarder TLS block here for your ops team:

---
forwarder_tls:
  mode: mTLS
  client_cert: /etc/forwarder/certs/client.crt
  client_key: /etc/forwarder/certs/client.key
  ca_bundle: /etc/forwarder/certs/ca.pem
  server_name: collector.internal.velox
---

We can also provide a validated Splunk HEC mapping if that's the final collector. Happy to jump on a quick screenshare to walk your infra team through the initial firewall window.

- Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Sr. Product Manager, Observability — Redwood Inference

- For the OTLP option: we'd prefer the OTel collector inside our VPC to keep traces local and reduce cross-checks. Will Redwood accept OTLP on loopback only? (your note suggested yes, wanted to confirm there is no outbound requirement in that mode)

If those are green we will provision a subnet and a single test forwarder host today. Please send the minimal firewall checklist as a single doc we can hand to platform. Also, can you upload the small evidence manifest once you run the POC transfer?
